title: Trend-signal refinements (Baltas–Kosowski)
ask: Do published trend-signal refinements improve the book?
reason: Only the t-statistic signal passed. It cut trend turnover 20%.
hypothesis: A t-statistic trend signal, range-based vol or a correlation factor improves the trend sleeve.
question: Do the refinements in Baltas and Kosowski (2017/2020) improve the deployed book: a trend signal sized by its Newey-West t-statistic, a range-based volatility estimate, a correlation factor (two versions), a de-risk rule filtered by the stock-bond correlation, or correlation features for the meta-label model?
prior: Baltas and Kosowski report that the TREND rule cuts turnover by about a quarter at similar or better Sharpe, because weak trends get small positions instead of full ±1 bets.
citations: Baltas, N. & Kosowski, R. (2020). Demystifying Time-Series Momentum Strategies. SSRN 2140091.
Newey, W. & West, K. (1987). A Simple, Positive Semi-Definite, Heteroskedasticity and Autocorrelation Consistent Covariance Matrix. Econometrica 55(3).
method: Full deployed stack at 8% vol, 2007-01 → 2026-09-11; one change per trial vs the deployed BASE.
Pre-registered rules: Sharpe ≥ BASE − 0.02; turnover −15% or MaxDD +1 pp or Sharpe +0.03; no crisis window > 2 pp worse; sensitivity plateau; alpha gate PASS at the true trial count.
verdict_reason: Only the t-statistic trend signal passed every rule: Sharpe 1.193 → 1.242, trend turnover −20%, Deflated Sharpe 1.000 at 27 trials, every crisis window within 1 pp. It was promoted into the live book in v44. The volatility estimate, the correlation factor, the stock-bond filter and the correlation features failed (+0.012 Sharpe or less each); the paper's literal correlation factor, run as a diagnostic, lowered Sharpe to 1.07.
lessons: A published refinement can be real and still small; the turnover cut, not the Sharpe, was the main gain.
